summary: Join our course on climate change adaptation for humanitarian projects. Equip yourself with essential tools to help communities thrive in a changing environment
lede: Climate change adaptation for humanitarian projects helps teams identify climate exposure, vulnerability, and adaptive capacity, then turn those findings into practical decisions across the project cycle. You will work with hazard mapping, vulnerability matrices, scenario planning, and adaptation prioritization to design measures suited to real delivery constraints. The course builds practical skills for integrating adaptation into assessments, proposals, implementation plans, monitoring frameworks, and reporting. Through exercises, you will develop a climate risk register, adaptation action plan, climate-sensitive logframe, adaptation indicators, and donor-ready results narrative.
audienceIntro: This climate change adaptation for humanitarian projects course is designed for professionals who need to integrate climate resilience into real project decisions, reporting lines, and field operations.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of humanitarian project design, implementation, or monitoring. Familiarity with project logframes, basic risk assessment, and proposal development is helpful, but no programming is required. Experience with field assessments, community engagement, or MEAL processes will help you apply the exercises more quickly. Advanced climate science is not required; the course focuses on operational application for humanitarian projects.
